claim: UnCert-CoT uses entropy-based and probability-differential-based confidence measures computed from the LLM's own next-token output distribution to decide whether to activate multi-path CoT reasoning during code generation, treating this expressed uncertainty as a compute-routing signal rather than a user-facing confidence report.
stance_target: expressed/log-prob-based uncertainty is usable and useful for internal routing decisions even without being validated as a calibrated correctness estimate
scope_conditions: code generation with LLM-based CoT reasoning, MHPP benchmark
quoted_support: We propose two confidence-based uncertainty measures: Entropy-based and Probability Differential-based methods. When uncertainty is high, UnCert-CoT activates CoT-decoding to generate multiple reasoning paths and selects the final code that exhibits the highest likelihood of correctness.
numbers: up to 6.1% improvement in PassRate accuracy on MHPP

claim: Standard CoT reasoning applied uniformly to all code-generation tasks exhibits 'overthinking', wasting tokens on easy problems and sometimes leading to incorrect reasoning paths, motivating uncertainty-gated selective reasoning.
stance_target: motivation for the paper's gating mechanism -- background on inefficiency of undifferentiated CoT
scope_conditions: code generation with LLMs applying CoT uniformly
quoted_support: existing CoT methods often exhibit a tendency toward "overthinking", where the LLM consistently applies reasoning strategies without adequately considering the task's underlying complexity.

claim: The paper does not report AUROC or calibration metrics of its entropy/probability-differential uncertainty measures against ground-truth functional correctness -- efficacy is validated only via downstream pass-rate improvement, not via direct correctness-prediction accuracy.
stance_target: the assumption that existing 'expressed uncertainty' methods have already been calibration-tested against internal sampling-based correctness signals
scope_conditions: based on abstract framing of UnCert-CoT's evaluation methodology
quoted_support: Our experimental results demonstrate that UnCert-CoT significantly enhances code generation accuracy on challenging benchmark MHPP... it achieves improvements up to 6.1% on PassRate accuracy.
